note.en: What you see: At the upper BLUE point on the front chest, the probe shows rib shadows with the pleural line between them. In the A profile the line slides with horizontal reverberation artefacts and no vertical B lines, marking dry aerated lung. In the B profile three or more vertical laser like B lines erase the horizontal artefacts and move with breath, marking interstitial fluid. Mixed A and B patterns localise the boundary of involvement.

steps.en: What you see: At the upper BLUE point on the front chest, the probe shows rib shadows with the pleural line between them. In the A profile the line slides with horizontal reverberation artefacts and no vertical B lines, marking dry aerated lung. In the B profile three or more vertical laser like B lines erase the horizontal artefacts and move with breath, marking interstitial fluid. Mixed A and B patterns localise the boundary of involvement.
Landmarks to confirm: Rib shadows, pleural line, horizontal reverberation artefacts in the A profile, three or more B lines in the B profile.

Common mistakes and correction: Calling two isolated B lines a B profile: the threshold is three or more per space. Missing sliding by holding the probe over rib: centre a rib space. Mistaking subcutaneous air for B lines: true B lines arise at the pleural line and move with breath.

Normal values with units: No numeric threshold applies beyond the B line count. Fewer than three B lines per space with preserved sliding is the normal A profile. Three or more B lines per space in two or more zones on both sides marks diffuse interstitial involvement and needs senior review.

Pitfalls: Focal B lines occur in contusion, infarct and early consolidation, so map every zone rather than judging one space. Absent sliding with B lines points toward consolidation rather than oedema. In breathless patients integrate the lung pattern with the heart and cava views before giving diuretics or fluids.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: Place the probe lengthwise at the upper BLUE point on the front chest with the marker toward the head. Find the pleural line in a rib space and watch a full breath for sliding. Count vertical B lines across the space: fewer than three keeps the A profile, three or more makes the B profile. Record the pattern, then move to the lower point. Compare with the opposite chest before concluding.

remember.en: Map the pattern across zones before judging

q.en: What defines the normal A profile?

o.en: Sliding with horizontal artefacts and fewer than three B lines

why.en: The A profile is sliding with horizontal reverberation and fewer than three B lines.

q.en: How many B lines per space make a B profile?

why.en: Three or more B lines per rib space marks the B profile.

q.en: A B profile appears in one zone only. What next?

o.en: Map every zone and integrate with heart and cava views
Give diuretics on one B profile alone

why.en: Focal B lines have several causes, so map all zones and integrate before treating.
